title: Gaussian Process Posterior Uncertainty for Causal Means at Critical Smoothness
banked_reason: D0.5 BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: mathematically sound and all seven sources verified; subfield paper-score ceiling 7.0 below field floor 7.4, no bounded in-scope fix; independent main validity gate confirms downgrade.
gap_reasons: The delivered result establishes the critical-regime conditional Gaussian limit, independently constructed susceptibility variance, and translated-interval coverage formula; it does not complete the calibration frontier.

Applicability remains restricted to one covariate, exactly known uniform design, the specified squared-exponential prior, and reciprocal-sample-size correlation length, with no theorem connecting this regime to the motivating application's fitted prior.

The worked computation encloses a finite-window susceptibility, but supplies neither an informative certified infinite-volume value nor evidence that the conservative evaluation procedure is practically usable.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the unchanged critical-bandwidth posterior Gaussian limit, independently constructed susceptibility with certified finite-window computation, efficient original-record centering, and own-quantile coverage with an open strict-undercoverage region. Primary-source gaps were repaired with Johnsen's closed covariance operator theorem and a proved paper-owned Sobolev closure bridge; the final math panel passed and all seven citations were verified. The global over-calibration/equality frontier remains open and the narrow design/prior regime plus uninformative infinite-volume evaluation cap the package at subfield; formalization did not start.
tldr: For the full one-dimensional H\"older-\(3/10\) causal class with public uniform design, the unchanged centered critical Bernoulli-logistic GP posterior has a uniform Gaussian limit with a positive susceptibility variance and certified finite-window approximation. An explicit credited second-order center is uniformly efficient, but the translated posterior-own \(90\%\) interval has limiting coverage \(2\Phi(z_{.95}\sqrt{v_\kappa(P)/V(P)})-1\), strictly below \(.90\) for \(\kappa>\sqrt\pi/6\). The class lies above the reported higher-order estimation boundary \(3/10>1/4\), below the separate first-order benchmark \(3/8<1/2\), and outside Ray--van der Vaart's Corollary 1 sufficient guarantee: \(3/10<1/2\) and no prior exponent satisfies \(1/2<\bar\beta<1/10\). These are three distinct comparisons, not an extension of their Bayesian theorem. Existence of a strict over-calibration region remains open.
gap: The closest binary causal GP results obtain calibration through concentration and prior-shift control or through adjusted posterior draws. Direct GP approximation and credible-set theorems impose different smoothing, contraction, likelihood or transformation requirements. They do not supply this original centered finite-occupancy critical-bandwidth law.
fill: The focal objects are the conditional logistic susceptibility, its certified evaluator with a rational finite-window checkpoint and separate error budgets, and its gap from known-distribution efficiency. The full specified law class and every positive compact bandwidth interval are retained. The efficient original-record center uses credited higher-order estimation support.
